Editor: Makers, "Where it makes its things": Paint where…, Rub out…, Nothing painted; the brush dragged on the land, [ and ], Esc; the edge of what is painted drawn on the land in the maker's colour. |
| One thing given a design, a size | The host's `one_design` (`design`, `scale`): for a thing of a wood, a meadow or a street the maker keeps it in its parameter `each`, by the thing's key; for a thing put down by itself it is that thing's own. It stays the thing it was (where it was moved to, its name), through another count, reach or set of designs; while the maker makes nothing under that key it waits. A size is the thing's footprint and `scale` in what is asked of it: its shape and what it is to walk into are made that size (not a house; not what has bones). |
| One more for an arrangement | The host's `add_one` (`design`, `pos`): kept in the maker's parameter `added`, each with a name (`added#a1`). It is listed with what the maker made, moved and removed with it, stays through another seed, and is moved, turned, resized and given another design like any thing of it. Taken away, it is no longer added (not kept away), and what was done to it goes with it. Not Duplicate, which is as it was: a thing by itself. |
| Listed and put back | `changes` lists them with the records ("given a design", "resized", "added"); `restore` takes one or all of a sort back; `nodes` counts them (`by_hand`). Makers shows the counts and a button for each. |
| One thing shaped alone | The host's `one_own`: a kind of the name asked for is written after what the thing is (one of the code's as `design_own` writes it; a kind of the world's by its text, each mesh written again under a name of its own), and that one thing is given it: one edit. Nothing else is of it. Makers: "Shape this one only…" does it and takes hold of its corners; "Shape its design 'X' (all N of it)…" is the other intention, beside it. |
| What is being shaped, seen and said | `handles.gd`: the strip's first line is whose shape it is (`scope`): SHAPING ONE THING ONLY, or SHAPING THE DESIGN 'X': EVERY thing of it changes, all N that stand (the host's `handles` says the kinds a mesh is the shape of and how many things of them stand). The shape's edges are drawn in the colour of the one thing picked; every corner is a dot (up to 1,500 corners); one line of how to use it. A mesh held is now found among a maker's things too. Designs: "Shape it in the view…" (with none standing, the next click puts one down and takes hold of it), and "Make it mine" says that it made a copy nothing is of, and what to do next. |
| Selection colours | `tint.gd`: six things a mark is for (a maker, one thing, the others of its arrangement, what is new, a handle, a sketch) and four choices of colours for them, the first as it always was. Every mark of `marks.gd` and `handles.gd` asks there; the words on the bar and in Makers say the colour chosen. Window > Colours; kept in `user://editor.cfg` on this machine, never with a world. |
| Five designs for a conifer wood | `conifer` (six sorts: a tall spruce, a broad fir, a pine bare below its crown, a young one, one the wind has had, an old fir), `mushroom` (3), `wildflower` (4: spikes of bloom), `fern` (3), `cones` (2: cones, acorns). Each a shape the code makes (`land.rs`), each a design in the one list: placed, given to a maker, made a kind. A conifer is flat faces in tiers, each face a little other in colour, lighter up and at the tips: read by its outline. Added after the twenty, so every number a world was written with means what it did. |
| A style says what stands | Two words of a style's `growth`: `trees DESIGNS` and `strewn DESIGNS`, written as a maker's `of` is. A wood or a meadow given no designs of its own is made of those (`Given::read`'s `usual`); given its own, of its own. The style **evergreen** (`styles.txt`): `trees conifer*7, tree 2`, `strewn grass*6, fern*4, wildflower*2, mushroom*2, cones, rock, bush`, its own colours and day. A wood keeps its places and names in it. Environment lists every style by name. |

**Decided.** Written into amendment 7j: where a maker makes its things is a reach, a
level or a painted area, each its own; what a maker keeps of single things is its own
data (`each`, `added`), not the core's `Add` record, which says a place and not what
a thing is; a shape is never kept on an instance apart from a design, so one thing
shaped alone has a design of its own; a style gives designs as a person does; selection
colours are roles.

**Checked.** *The build:* the host builds in release with no warning. *Tests of what
changed* (host, release, one at a time, run after the last change to the host): 22
unit and **41 protocol tests pass**. New: **p39** (a plateau; each tree on the ground
under it at every reach; a reach drawn in keeps the thickness, said, undone as one;
kept to its level on top and, moved, at the foot; painted: there and nowhere else,
named for where, no ground made again; painted further, none has moved; more of them,
every one that stood; rubbed out; a tree taken away and one moved still those trees;
turned; copied and removed with its paint, and back; written and opened; cleared; a
meadow painted; three things refused), **p40** (one tree made a rock, another a kind
and bigger, a third smaller, each the thing it was through another count and other
designs, waiting while its place is not made; one more added, kept through another
seed and a move of the maker, itself moved and given a design; written and opened;
taken away, undone; put back singly and by sort, with nothing left waiting; a thing
put down given a design and a size; a duplicate standing alone; one tree and one tent
made their own, the mesh held said to be one thing's, no other tree made again;
five things refused), **p41** (25 designs with their sorts; the twenty numbered as they
were; every conifer taller for its width than any broadleaf and each its own height;
a wood and a meadow unchanged with no style and with a style that says nothing of
them; in one that does, conifers at the same places under the same names and the
open ground as strewn; a maker's own designs over the style's; three wrong lines
said; no style again, as it was). p37's count of designs changed from 21 to 26.
*The way of working, with the mouse and the keys:* `-Tour -Only region` (new: a wood
clicked onto a plateau and standing where it was clicked; its reach dragged to 14 m
at the rim, on its level; the box; a stroke painted, one undo, redone; one tree a
rock, twice as big; one more added and a duplicate standing alone; one shaped alone
with a corner dragged; the colours chosen from the bar, every mark that colour, the
choices told apart from each other and from three greens by number, kept in a file
and read again; the style picked from the bar and taken off) passed three times, the last
after every change to the scripts. Its first run ended with the editor falling over
as it closed (code 0xC0000005, after every check had passed): the colours were told
of a change by functions kept in a list that outlived what they held; they are now
looked at each frame instead, and no run since has ended so. *Beside it, after the
last change to the interface:* `designs`, `editing`, `chosen`, `handles`, `kinds`
passed (each also once before it), and `makers` passes to its end after being put
right (above), three times; each with no script error. *Beside it, before the last
small changes* (the size of the corner dots, two wordings, a line in Keys): `roof`,
`growth`, `firstwalk`, `land`, `meshes` passed, once each. `ui` passed eight runs
of ten after one expectation was changed to the new words; the two failures are
under "Known gaps". The demo `region -Check`: 5 beats of 5, run again after the last
change. *Worlds written before:*
copies of `editor/my world.json` and `editor/world.json` opened by the host as
committed and by this one, and everything every maker made written out (2,654 and
2,312 lines): **the same, line for line**, with nothing needing a look. The two files
and `feel.cfg` are byte for byte what they were. **Not run:** the whole tour; the
tour's other parts; the core's tests (the core was not changed); `-Measure`, `-Weigh`;
the built game. **Not tried by hand: none of it.**

**Not done.**

- **A painted area is squares 2 m a side**, with a hard edge; it is drawn as its
  outline, not filled; and it is one maker's (two makers are painted twice).
- **A level is one band about the maker's middle**: two plateaus of a height within
  one reach both have it. There is no area by slope, by surface, or by distance from
  a road or the water beyond what a wood already had.
- **A wood painted names its places anew** (`tree#a…`): what was moved or taken away
  before, by hand, waits under the old names and is back when the paint is cleared.
  The same as a meadow given designs.
- **Keeping the thickness can leave a hand-changed thing waiting**: a wood drawn in
  has fewer places, and a tree moved by hand whose place is no longer made waits (it
  is listed, and is back with the reach).
- **A size is of the whole thing**, one number: not taller without wider, no colour,
  no other number of its own. A house is not resized; nor is what has bones.
- **"Shape this one only" on a kind that is "like" another** and has its mesh from it
  is refused, with why. A thing made its own keeps the name `NAME-own`; the designs
  made so are not gathered or cleaned up, and are listed under "Yours" like any.
- **A street given designs still has no houses** (D1): the requirement that replaces
  it is written (principle Q), not built.
- **The corners of a shape are dots only up to 1,500 corners**; a tree written out has
  about 1,200, which is many dots. A roof of thousands has its edges only.
- **A line's own marks** (the places of a road, dragged) are orange and yellow
  whatever colours are chosen; the land's brush likewise.
- **The colours chosen are not applied in a session a demo began** (a demo reads no
  file of the machine's): they are the next time the editor is started plainly.
- **A style names only designs every world has**, for the whole world; its two lines
  are written in `styles.txt`, not in the editor. A meadow in such a style names its
  things `grown#`, as when it is given designs.
- **The conifers are code**: six outlines, no parts a person sets, no branches, a
  wind that moves them by height only. They are not E1b. A kind made after one ("Make
  it mine") does not move in the wind, like every kind made so.
- **Mushrooms, ferns and cones are small**: from far off they are colour on the
  ground, and are seen for what they are near to.
- Not the whole tour. Not tried by hand.


### The island town, and what lives in it (2026-10-11)

Asked for by the user as their main place to try the editor in: a small, coherent,
playable town on the test island, with houses that are not one house, a shop, two
surgeries and a church, gardens, a pond that is alive, animals, a woodcutter and a few
townspeople; all of it left as a world that can go on being shaped, nothing of it a
scene of its own. The optional part (more movement, an obstacle course) was to be
begun only after the town was built, saved, opened and tested, and is **deferred**:
see "Movement" below.

**The world.** `editor\town.json`, built by `editor\town.ps1`. It is the island of the
playground (seed 3), three lines (Main Street, Church Lane, Pond Lane), and 57 makers
that made 1985 things. It is opened with `editor\run.ps1 -World editor\town.json`.
`town.ps1` does not write over a town that is there (`-Over` does, keeping the one
there was in `editor\backups` first).

**How it was built, and why that way.** `editor/host/examples/town.rs` says to the host,
one after another, the commands the editor says when a person works: `begin` with the
lines and the land, `kind` and `mesh` for each design, `sculpt` (flatten, paint, bare)
for the churchyard, the house sites and the pond, `place`, `add` for each maker,
`add_one` for each thing of a garden, `param`, `delete` for the houses a road or a
building is in the way of, `write`. 1197 commands, about a second. So the town is
made of nothing the editor cannot make or change, and what is left is a world file
like any other. The script is the town's alone; it is a hand that does not tire, not
a generator, and nothing reads it afterwards.

| What | Where | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| The designs: 60 kinds and meshes a person can read and change. Roofs (gable either way, hip, lean, spire); cottage, cottage_slate, cabin, townhouse, farmhouse; store, vet, doctor, church; flowerbed, vegpatch, herbs, berrybush, picket, stepstone, stump, logpile, beehive, birdbath, trough; pondwater, lilypad, lily, reeds; horse, horse_grey, cow, cow_brown, goat, dog, dog_collie, tomcat, mouser, rabbit, squirrel; bird (three), butterfly (three), bee, dragonfly, frog, fish (two), duck; villager, woodcutter, shopkeeper, gatherer, gardener, caller, parson | `editor/godot/town.txt` (text, as `cast.txt` is) | test `p42` (every one written into a world with nothing not understood); demo pictures |
| The town built by commands, written, opened again and written again: the same file, byte for byte | `editor/host/examples/town.rs`, `editor/town.ps1` | the build itself (it stops if the two files differ) |
| What is alive and has no body: content says `flutters R H [V]`, `swims R H [LEAP]`, `hops R` or `perches R`, and while the world runs it is drawn going about so, in place of where it was made. A frog leaps from the walker; a bird sits in the top of a tree within reach and flies to another | host: trait words in `shapes/kind.rs`, said in `shapes.rs`; `editor/godot/wild.gd` (new); `things.gd` `said` | test `p42`; tour `-Only town` (32 that flutter, 9 that swim, 5 that hop, 15 that perch; 15 birds up in trees; none that swims out of the pond or off its depth; a frog 1.34 m from where it sat after the walker came) |
| Standing water as a thing: a kind that says `sheer` is drawn seen through; one that says `water R H` is water for what hops to rest on. A pond is a hollow made with the land's flatten tool and one such thing put down in it; its edge is where the land comes up through the sheet | `world_view.gd` (`GLASS`, chosen in `_build`), `wild.gd` `_rest`, kind `pondwater` | tour `-Only town` (the walker put down in the pond stands on its bed, 0.00 m off); demo pictures (fish and lily stems seen under the water) |

They go to one of that sort within R metres of home, stand off it, turn to it, do the move again and again for S seconds, and go to another; several lines, each sort in turn. The woodcutter says `tends tree 30 chop 9`, the gatherer `tends wildflower 26 stoop 4` and two more, the gardener the beds, the caller the three doors | `folk.gd` (`of_sort`, `_tend`, `_tending`); set `worker` in `moves.txt` | tour `-Only town` (the woodcutter seen in `chop` 1.15 m from a tree and facing it squarely; the gatherer in `stoop` at a flower) |
| Six sets of moves for animals on the sheep's bones (horse, cow, goat, dog, rabbit, squirrel): the sheep's moves by other numbers | `moves.txt` | demo (they stand, stray and graze); tour `flock`, `cast`, `keeper` still pass |
| A way asked from ground not yet made walkable is not asked of the server (it answered with an error for each of many) | `nav.gd` `path` | tour `keeper` |

**The town, in a list.**
- *Streets:* Main Street (15 houses of the street maker, with doors that open; lamps,
  fences, barrels, carts from the furniture maker), Church Lane (6 houses that are
  designs: cottage, cottage_slate, cabin, townhouse), Pond Lane (a lane and no street).
- *About the crossroads:* the general store (brick, a false front, a striped awning on
  posts, a board), the doctor's (white, red tiles, a porch, a red cross), the vet's
  (white boards, a green hipped roof, a half door, a paw on a board, a rail); the
  green (a well, three benches, three trees, two beds, two stalls, a bird bath, a
  signpost, lamps); things outside the shop.
- *The church* on levelled ground at the head of Church Lane: nave, buttresses,
  windows, tower, belfry, spire, cross; yews behind it.
- *Three properties:* Rose Cottage and its garden (four beds, a path of six stones, a
  fence with a gap, a bench, a bird bath, shrubs, flowers, herbs, butterflies); the
  woodcutter's cabin and yard (two vegetable patches, three berry bushes, herbs, two
  piles of logs, a stump, a hatchet, two hives and their bees); the farmhouse and its
  yard (haystacks, a cart, a trough, a well, fences, beds, a patch).
- *The pond:* six overlapping hollows with a level bed, sand about it; the water; 13
  pads and lilies, 16 clumps of reeds, rocks, a bench, two trees; 7 fish, 2 ducks, 5
  frogs, 3 dragonflies, 4 birds.
- *What grows:* Home Wood, Hill Wood, West Copse, the churchyard yews; ferns,
  mushrooms and cones under Home Wood; four meadows and a patch of wildflowers.
- *Animals:* 7 sheep (the flock maker), 4 horses, 5 cows, 4 goats, 7 rabbits, 6
  squirrels, 3 dogs, 2 cats, 15 birds, 16 butterflies, 13 bees.
- *People:* the woodcutter, the gatherer, the gardener, the shopkeeper, the caller,
  the parson, two of the town who stray and wave.

**How it is kept, for whoever changes it.** A building, a person, a cat or the pond's
water is one thing put down (its own row in Makers, named). A herd, the rabbits, the
birds of the wood, the butterflies are each a **meadow given designs** (`the horses`:
`horse*2, horse_grey`): how many, how far, and of what are its settings, and one more
is added by hand. A garden, the green, what stands in and about the pond are each a
**meadow that makes nothing itself** (count 0) to which every thing was added with
"Add one thing by hand": so a garden is one maker, moved, copied and removed whole,
and each bed in it is one thing. That is the nearest the editor has to a group (D3),
and it is used as one here; it is called a meadow in Makers, which is the engine's
word and not the right one.

**What is the town's alone, and what is general.** General, for any world: the four
words for what is alive without a body, `sheer` and `water`, `tends`, the six sets of
moves, and every design in `town.txt` (written into another world by the same build
script, or pasted into Kinds and meshes one at a time). The town's alone: the build
script, and where everything stands. **Not reachable from the editor:** there is no
button that writes `town.txt`'s designs into the world open (cast.txt has "Add the
examples"; the town's are in the town); and the build script is run from a terminal.

**Houses: what was done, and what a house engine would need.** The house a street
builds is still one shape (a box, a gable, a door on one side, windows by the bay) in
other sizes and colours: its generator is the identity prototype's, and to give it a
second roof or a second floor is to change the facade planner, the inside, the
collider and what saved worlds are made of. That was not done. What was done is the
other way the engine already had: **a house as a design**, parts and meshes written
as text, given to the same street maker (`of`). Four that differ in outline, not in
paint: a low thatched cottage with a steep roof and an end chimney; a log cabin with
a low roof, an outside chimney and a porch on posts; a tall house, stone below and
timbered above, jettied, under a hipped roof; a farmhouse with a wing forward under
its own gable. And the civic four. Their limits are a design's: they are not gone
into (no door, no inside); what is walked into is one box about all of it (the walker
stops at a porch's edge, not its posts); a `like` changes colours and adds parts but
has no numbers ("two floors", "a porch: yes"). A house engine (amendment E2) would
want: a plan of rooms or at least a footprint of more than one box; storeys; roof
forms as a choice (gable, hip, lean, with the ridge either way); openings placed by
rule on each face; porches, chimneys and wings as parts with their own numbers; an
inside and doors that open; a collider that follows the parts; and all of it as a
design's parameters, so that "cottage" and "tall house" are two settings of one thing.

**Movement, as it stands; the optional part.** What the walker can do today, all of
it from before this pass and none of it changed: walk, run, a jump that is higher held
longer, a running jump, a long jump into a roll, a dash on the ground and in the air,
a dodge, a quick step to either side, crouch, a hard landing and one rolled out of,
swimming afloat, **an edge caught, hung from and climbed, a wall held to and slid
down, and a jump off a wall** (`ledge_hang`, `climb`, `wall_grip`, `wall_jump`:
`run.ps1 -Demo climb`). Not there: a wall caught again straight from a wall jump as a
move of its own (it may already happen, since a wall is caught whenever a way is asked
into one while falling: not tried), and a backward flip. **The obstacle course and
the new moves were not begun.** The town came first as asked; what was left of the
pass went to checking it. The honest next step is small: a course of plain blocks
(kinds with their own solid) away from the town, a tour part that tries wall to wall
on it, and then whichever move that shows to be missing, written in `moves.txt` and
`poses.txt` as the others are.

**Not done, and limits to know.**
- While editing, what flutters, swims, hops and perches stands where it was put: a
  bird and a butterfly on the ground, a fish on the pond's bed. They go about only in
  Play. Nothing of them is saved with a game.
- They have no bones: a wing beat is the whole thing made narrower and wider. A fish
  keeps to its pond because its kind says how far it swims (4.5 m), not because it
  knows where the water ends: put in a smaller pond it swims through the bank.
- The woodcutter cuts nothing: no tree falls, nothing is gathered, his axe is a part
  of him and not a thing held. The gatherer takes nothing. `tends` is going, turning
  and a move; what the move does to the thing is behaviour (amendment 7g, M4).
- The animals go by the sheep's poses at other sizes: a horse walks as a big sheep
  walks, a rabbit does not hop, a squirrel does not climb. A dog and a cat stray and
  do not go to anyone.
- Pond water is one level sheet nine metres out, as big as its kind says. From far
  off (where things are drawn together) it is not seen through. It casts no ripple
  and nothing floats on it by the host's own rule (`floats` is the sea's): a pad
  stands on a stem as long as the water is deep.
- A design's building is not gone into.
- Near a road a meadow makes nothing (4.6 to 13.5 m from it, where houses stand), so
  a herd or butterflies by a lane must be added by hand to a garden's maker.
- The standalone game was not built from the town (`export.ps1` builds from
  `editor\world.json`): deferred, as asked.

**Checks run** (2026-10-11): the host built; all host tests one at a time, 22 and 42,
passed, `p42` new; `-Tour -Only town`, twice, no problems (a frame on the green 1.8
ms, 882 draw calls, 2.3 million triangles; opened in half a second; written and
opened again with the same fingerprint and the same count; the town's file, both of
the person's worlds and `feel.cfg` unwritten); `-Tour -Only flock`, `cast`, `keeper`,
no problems (`keeper` failed once, on the set `folk` having been given `chop`: that is
why the woodcutter has a set of his own, and `folk` is as it was. Its run before that
printed no result at all: host tests were being built beside it, which was my doing,
and the build could not replace the host's program while it ran); `-Tour -Only ui`, once, after the checklist was written anew, no problems;
`-Demo town -Check`, three times, the last on the code as committed, its 25 pictures
looked at. **Not run:** the whole tour; `-Measure`, `-Weigh`; the built game.

### The training ground, the children and the old tractor (2026-10-11)

Asked for by the user after the town: "proceed with obstacle course and wall to wall
check. add a basic parkour moveset to the character and build the course to showcase
it. include it somewhere on the island where the demo town is. also add some children
running around playing with bubbles and basic toys to the island. and a basic old
rusty farm tractor parked somewhere covered in ivy and moss and critters."

All of it is in `editor\town.json`, which was built again by `editor\town.ps1 -Over`
(68 makers, 2049 things; the town as it was built before is in `editor\backups`, and
in git). Nothing was tried by hand.

**Wall to wall, checked first.** It worked as the moves were: nothing was written for
it. Between two walls 2.6 m apart the walker, held to one (`wall_grip`), jumps off it
toward the other (`wall_jump`: 1.5 m up, 2.4 m out), meets it while still rising, and
is held to it at the top of the jump, 1.5 m higher than before. Held at 1.29, 2.78
and 4.27 m; the fourth jump brings the top of a 7 m tower within reach of the hands,
which catch it (`ledge_hang`), and it is climbed. What it needs of the person: the
way asked toward the *other* wall when jump is pressed.

| What | How | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| **Something low gone over at a run** (`vault`) | `moves.txt`: `upon low`, `when ground running pressing`; up beside the edge in 0.13 s (`to above`), then 1.7 m over it in 0.22 s, flat, and out at 0.9 of that speed. `grasp.gd` feels for what is low on the ground (`find(..., low)`: an edge between 0.3 m and `ledge_low` above the feet, nothing at the chest, room beyond), and `motor.gd` asks it only of a body that is running and whose set has a move that begins `upon low`. `poses.txt` `vault/up` (the hands on the edge), `vault/over` | tour `course`: three rails 0.9 m high and 4 m apart gone over in 2.5 s from standing, never under 5 m/s between them |
| **A step up a wall** (`wall_run`) | `moves.txt`: `asks jump`, `when air wall pressing aloft 1`; 1.25 m up the wall in 0.32 s, kept to it (`to wall`), and it lets an edge be caught or a jump off cut in. A jump's rise lets it cut in, and so does a hold to a wall (before `wall_jump`: into the wall goes up it, any other way pushes off). `poses.txt` `wall_run` | tour `course`: the 4.4 m wall, held to at 1.28 m by a jump alone and its edge not caught; then stepped up, the edge caught with feet at 2.68 m, climbed, stood on at 4.4 m |
| **A backflip** | `moves.txt`: `asks jump`, `when ground crouch still`, `heads off`, `faces same`; 1.45 m up and 1.9 m back in 0.66 s. `poses.txt` `backflip/flight` says `tumble -1` | tour `course`: rose 1.45 m, went 2.07 m back, stands, faces as it did |

**What changed for the walker everywhere, and is the user's to keep or not:**

- At a run, a garden fence, a bench or a crate is gone over without being asked.
- Held to a wall, jump with the way asked going into the wall is a step up it (once
  until the ground); with no way asked or any other, it pushes off as before.
- Crouched with no way asked, jump is a backflip. It was a long jump the way it faced.

Each is taken away by deleting its name from `set walker` in `moves.txt`. `feel.cfg`
was not changed and no number was added to it: the new moves' numbers are written
out in `moves.txt`.

**Not done:**

- **A slide under something, a run along a wall, a swing from a bar.** Each needs
  code the moves' words do not reach: a body that is lower while it slides (the
  capsule is one height), a wall felt for to the side, something to hang from that
  is not an edge.
- The course's pieces are right for the numbers `feel.cfg` has now (a jump 1.3 m,
  hands 2.15 m above the feet, a wall jump 2.4 m out). They are not made from them.
- The pillars are jumped at a walk: at a run the jump overshoots them. Nothing
  slows a run for a short jump.
- A child at a toy stoops to it or cheers, and the toy is as it was. The children
  knock the balls about only by running into them.
- Bubbles rise where they were put whether or not the girl is blowing.
- Children are a person's shape made smaller: the head is not bigger for the body.
- The tractor's ivy does not move in the wind, its robin does not fly, and its
  wheels are eight-sided. It cannot be driven.
- A vault's first part (0.13 s up beside the edge) is slow across the ground: over
  the whole of three rails the walker keeps 5 m/s or more only between them.
- Nobody but the walker goes over, up or between anything.

  - Buttons changed in the Project window go into the layout in use (one undo each); your own buttons (the in-game kind) are not touched from there.
  - While trying here the layout comes first; in a game on its own, the player's own changes do.
- **Presses** (`inputs.txt` `press`, `inputbook.gd`, `presses.gd`):
  - **Ways of pressing:** pressed, let go, held down, tapped, held a while, pressed twice, toggled, repeated, buttons in a row, and chords (LB+X, Ctrl+E).
  - **Only while** a condition holds, **for** a character, by **priority**.
  - **What a press does:** a button of the game, a move, a power, an item (hand, hip, pack, swap), a wheel and its quick one, a state (crawl), the world map, words.
  - **One button never does two things:** a button a press could happen on is taken from the ordinary actions meanwhile (`Controls.claimed`). A tap waits for a double-press window if one is written.
  - **Toggles** hold a button (`Controls.forced`) until pressed again or their `ends` holds; they are shown while playing.
  - **New conditions** (`cond.gd`): `holds`, `wears`, `keeps`, `is STATE`, `ready`, `has_target`.
  - **Crawl** (`intent.crawl`, `motor.gd`) is low, slow and shows the crawling clip; jump stands up from it.
- **Wheels** (`inputs.txt` `wheel`, `wheel.gd`):
  - **Slots** round from the top, wheels inside wheels; `powers` and `items` fill one with what the player has.
  - **Pointing:** the stick, the mouse or the arrow keys.
  - **Chosen by** letting go, confirming, or made the quick one only; what can't be used is shown with why, or hidden.
  - **Time:** unchanged, held (the game's own hold), or slowed and eased back (`factor` times `physics.txt` speed, in `loose.gd`).
- **World › Project › Controls & Input** (`controlspage.gd`): Layouts & buttons, Presses, Wheels (*Try it* over the editor), Test (what was heard and why), Problems.
- **World › Project › Worlds** (`worldspage.gd`):
  - every world file (19), the one being edited read live;
  - ways out and in by the thing that says `leads`, both ways or one, to no world;
  - the catalogue and a map of connections;
  - Go to it, Open it, Play beside it.
- **Maps** (`maps.gd`):
  - a mini map (`hud.txt` `piece minimap`: reach, turns, round), the land from above with ways, quest marks, foes and the player;
  - a world map on Back held or the full stop, the game held, moved and brought nearer.
- **ITS ANIMATION** on an ability's and a move's page: the move, each part's clip, *Edit the move in the Character Studio*, *Import animations…*, *Animation packs →*.
- **Assets:** Kenney's Input Prompts 1.5 (CC0) in `downloads-untrustedinput-prompts`, 141 pictures in `editorgodotglyphs` (`glyphs.gd`), credited.
- **Checked by:** `-Demo inputs` (new, 15 beats, features: protected): 15/15, no problems, no script errors, no damage. It took three runs:
  - **first:** the talk's `open` was read as a flag, so no press was heard (986 script errors);
  - **second:** `loose.gd` set the time scale every frame over the wheel's;
  - **third:** the demo chose the Inspector's thing by Makers instead of the Inspector's list.

  - **fourth:** a bad escape in a string I wrote while mending the window's width.

### The Project window to the design; abilities of a character's own; buttons where they are listed; the aim mended (2026-10-23)

After the user's hand test of H1:
- run's button could not be changed (run was in Buttons, not among the moves, and Buttons changed nothing);
- an ability could not be given to the player without an item;
- the Who tab's bones and clip libraries said nothing;
- holding aim did not follow the camera, and the mark sat on the player's face.

The user then sent `Draw3D_Project_Window_Design.html` as what the window must look like ("WHY DO I HAVE TO TELL YOU HOW TO DO THIS SO MANY TIMES … sort out all the text stuff"). How each part matches Godot, Unity, Unreal, GameMaker and RPG Maker is in `Draw3D_Project_Window_Comparison_2026-10-23.md`.

- **World › Project, as the design lays it out** (`projectview.gd`):
  - **Top bar:** the project and its world, *Saved* or the count of unsaved changes, search across everything, ＋ Create.
  - **Left:** the categories (Overview, Worlds, Characters & Creatures, Assets & Objects, Abilities & Effects, Gameplay, Audio, Styles & Materials, Data & Libraries; Project Settings).
  - **Centre:**
    - the overview: the playable character and the active world at the top, then a tile per category with its count;
    - or a category as cards under headings: a picture in each sort's mark and colour (a status, shot or power in its own colour), its name, type · scope, and a tag (*The player has it*, *Used by N*, *N placed*, *Not used*, *Missing*), with filters for type and scope, and Cards or List;
    - or one thing's page, its form.
  - **Right:** Details (its definition in words, its scope), Assignments (who has or uses it, and how: "Ember rod — grants it while held", "Ranger — knows it once the quest … is done"), Dependencies (what it uses and what for), then Set it up here, Open in its editor, Preview, and the rest.
  - **Bottom:** where one is.
  - Debug is kept apart from Project Settings, as the design asks.
  - The window opens up to 1440 by 900.
- **＋ Create:** a character (a copy of the one played), a power, a shot, a status, an effect, a move or an item (made like another), each opened at once as its form; or a new world, or animations imported.
- **Abilities of a character's own** (`charbook.gd` `knows POWER [on BUTTON] [when CONDITION]`; `aim.gd` `known`, `cast_known`):
  - On the player's Abilities tab, *Give it this ability* gives the player a power with no item needed.
  - Its card sets *Pressed with* (Aim then Attack, its move's button, or any button) and *Had* (from the start, once a quest is done, once a quest is taken on; the quest picked).
  - In play, it is cast by its button at whom it picks, or aimed (hold Aim) and let go with Attack, with nothing to draw.
  - Items that grant a power are listed under it as cards.
- **Every button where it is listed:**
  - **Moves tab:** under its own moves, *Built into every character* lists run, jump, crouch, dash, the quick steps, attack, aim, lock, act, draw, recenter, use, out, light and greet, each with what presses it. One chosen shows its button card: the controller button picked from a list, *Press a new key…* (then the key), a mouse button picked, what else the same button presses, and *As the game first had it*.
  - **Buttons tab:** every button under its heading, each chosen shows the same card, and the player's moves on that button (✕ off, *Put this move on it*).
  - **A move:** says what presses its button, with *Change what presses it →*.
- **Who tab in plain words:** *Animation set-up (follows the model: rarely changed)* holds *Skeleton* and *Animations from*, each pack named with where it came from, with a line saying what they are for.
- **Forms for more sorts** (`shapes.gd`; H2 in part):
  - **Power:** what it does, showing only the fields that apply (the shot it throws, or how far around), harm, heals, the status it puts on, its move, when and where it is let go, rest, cost (what and how much), reach, whom it goes to, how many, apart, turning, its effects and sound; levels shown in words, set in Shots and powers.
  - **Shot:** shape, size, colour, glow, trail, speed, fall, time, turning, harm, status, push, burst, sounds.
  - **Status:** called, says, colour, effect, lasts, speed kept, no running, held still, harm taken, at most.
  - **Effect, sound:** what it is; how it looks or sounds, set in their windows.
  - **Quest:** called, how it is asked, thanks, afterwards, the sound, effect and move when it is done; its steps shown in words.
  - New field kinds: a part of a line (a shot's size and colour), a colour, an amount (a cost), what a power does, and fields shown only when they apply.
  - Pickers name each choice with a few words of what it is.
  - Lines further in (a quest's steps, a move's phases) are no longer counted as the entry's own.
- **The aim mended** (`aim.gd`, `eye.gd`): the aim was measured with the editor's camera, not the one played through, so it never followed where the player looked, in any eye. It is measured with the camera in use now. From behind, it takes what the middle of the view meets beyond the player, or as far as the aim reaches; while aiming, the eye comes in over the right shoulder (closer, narrower), so the mark is beside the player, not on them. The aim line ends where it is aimed.
- **Checked by**:
  - `-Demo hubplayer` (rewritten, 11 beats, features: protected): 11/11, no problems, no script errors, no damage, after one run that found the aim measured with the editor's camera. It covers:
    - the overview;
    - the Characters cards, and the player still listed under "this world's only";
    - the ember bolt's assignments (the ember rod grants it);
    - a power as its fields (the reach of one that goes around hidden);
    - its moves and the 16 built-in actions;
    - Dodge's button picked and undone;
    - run's controller button picked as LB, then put back as the game had it;
    - the frost bolt given with no item, had once a quest is done, both undone;
    - in play, the frost bolt cast with only an axe in hand, and the aim turning 69° as the eye turns 69°;
    - every button listed with its card;
    - Create › Ability opened as its form and undone.
  - Its pictures looked at; the browser's header and the right panel were too crowded at 1280 by 720 and were changed after.
  - Other demos not run, by the user's word (they test the level by hand). **Not tried by hand.**
- **Not done**:
  - talks, acts, recipes, goods and needs still open as text;
  - a quest's steps and a power's levels are not rows yet;
  - H3–H6 (kinds as prefabs with overrides, worlds and places, one event editor, Problems);
  - Versions & History is not in the window (the design: nothing shown that does not work);

After the user rejected World › Project as built the pass before ("I still don't see the option to change the player character … then it just has a bunch of text … this engine is essentially useless if I've got to go in and type text everywhere"), and sent an outside suggestion (Godot's scenes, nodes and resources; Unity's prefabs; Unreal's world scale; GameMaker's simplicity; RPG Maker's database). ### Emberwatch: The Last Beacon, a benchmark authored through the interface (2026-10-23)

At the user's brief: a 30-minute vertical slice (hamlet, survivors, ashfang wolves, the beacon, the night assault, endings), built in stages, **authored through the editor's own interface as a person would** and recorded as it was done. The records are:

- `Draw3D_Emberwatch_Benchmark.md`: the baseline, the route, the systems, the evaluation and the limitations;
- `Draw3D_Emberwatch_Authoring_Workflow.md`: each workflow, as performed, marked existing, exposed or new.

**How it is authored.** `editor\run.ps1 -Author emberwatch` runs `author.gd` (the interface driver) with `author_emberwatch.gd` (what to do) and `author_emberwatch_words.gd` (what is typed). It clicks the bar, the toolbar and the windows by their words, types into fields and text windows key by key, and clicks and drags in the view, all through Godot's input. It never calls the host or writes a file, and the real pointer is never moved. From an empty island to `editor/emberwatch.json`: about 650 steps, 196 s, each in `editor/godot/author-emberwatch.log`.

**Built in the engine, because the interface could not do it** (workflow document, section 9):
- *An hour of play lasts (minutes)* at the Player start (Inspector, World outline): the world fact `hour_lasts`, which a behaviour may change and a saved game keeps (`clock.gd`, `gameui.gd`, `makers.gd`, host `land.rs`, `lib.rs`).
- The `endings` text: endings chosen by condition, each with its own title and words, `{fact}` in them (`endbook.gd`, `gameui.gd`).
- A creature with a blow that a behaviour sends somewhere (`go`, `hurry`) breaks down a barricade in its way, and its `go` waits while it does (`fight.gd`, `rules.gd`).
- A drawn structure (a house, a paving) is a place by its name: the middle of what was drawn (host `lib.rs`).
- `Put one down` armed the kind by its row in a list that changed before the click; now it arms by name (`main.gd` `armed_kind`).
- The Texts window's *also the project's file* checkbox: unticked, a text applied is this world's alone (`textview.gd`).
- The kind line **`restless`** (Inspector: *far off too*): never let go by the regions, never left standing far away, and made wherever it stands. Without it the raiders waiting in their den were let go, left standing, or never made, so the raid never came, or came short (host `kind.rs`, `things.gd`, `folk.gd`, `inspect.gd`).
- `run.ps1 -Author NAME` (tooling).

**Found while authoring, not changed:** a thing put down is turned at random. Turning it means scrolling the Inspector to `>  Placement`, and the Inspector names it by its kind. A selected path's settings panel takes clicks meant for the land. There is no "raise to H metres", and no warning for slopes too steep to walk. A script-started editor ignores `-World`. These are in the benchmark, 4.2.

**Checked by script:**
- `-Demo emberwatch` (13 beats), the prepared route: Mara's quest, the Broken Gate, supplies, two gaps mended, a kit crafted and put down, F5/F9 keeping what was mended, Pip found, the ridge, the valve, the beacon repaired and lit, the night begun, the first run of wolves battering the north gate (10 blows, none through it while it stood), and dawn showing **Dawnkeeper**.
- `-Demo emberdark` (4 beats), the unprepared night: the gaps left broken, midnight bringing the assault with the beacon cold, the wolves inside and after Wren, and **Cold Valley**.
- Host tests: 189 passed.
- The regression demos for what changed (fights, shelter, bell, regions, remembers, perceives, inspect) all pass. `-Demo guard` fails, and fails the same way on the committed code (Known gaps).

**Not done:** the survivors are never harmed (they shelter indoors, and wolves open no doors), so The Hamlet Fell can't be reached. Embers in the Dark, the Hunter's Cache, the Farmer's Choice, Finn's hand-in and waves 2 and 3 are written but no demo plays them. Nothing has been tried by hand.

### G5, perception, ways and answering together (2026-10-22)

The last of the user's order (G3, PW0, G4, PW1, G6, G5), from the gameplay roadmap's G5 (`Draw3D_Gameplay_Roadmap_2026-10-21.md`): "deer flee the walker and a wolf; three guards respond to one alarm; a cat follows the walker up stairs", and thirty bodies measured. Much of it was there (`sees`, `near`, `flee` and `go` already took a name; `tell` already reached others; `follows` already made a pet keep by you): G5 widens those rather than adding a second system. Nothing of it is tried by hand.

**What was built.**
- **Whom, in words** (`cond.gd` `where_is`, `watch.gd` `counts_as`): wherever a behaviour or a design says whom (sees, near, flee, follow, face, go, tell, a design's `follows`, `shies`), it may say what they count as: `folk` (of a person's shape), `creature` (any other), `hunter` (what hunts, preys or fights), `anyone` (the walker too), or a word of their own `tags`; several with "or" (`flee walker or hunter`). The dead are no one.
- **`tags WORD ...`**: a new word of a design or of one thing's own lines (host `kind.rs`): what it counts as. The Inspector says what it means.
- **`on sees WHO [R]`**: heard once as it comes to see them, and again only after it has lost sight of them (`rules.gd`).
- **Heard at a run**: the folk and the creatures going faster than 3 m/s make steps that whatever hears hears, as what they are called and what they count as (`on hears dog`, `on hears creature`; `watch.gd` `_footfalls`).
- **`follow WHO [R]`**, a step: kept within R metres of them (3 if not said), after them by the ways there are, at a run when far behind; it goes on until another step is done instead.
- **Behaviours to use** (behaviours.txt): `follows` (whom, near), `looks_into_noises` (a noise heard: goes, looks about, goes home), `keeps_home` (wanders by day, home between the hours it keeps in). `deer_ways` fears `walker or hunter` (its `fears`); `skittish` runs from its `from`; `guard_ways` tells the alarm to its `calls_to` (anyone, as before, if not said).
- **`tell WORD [R] [to WHO]`**: told only to those it names (`tell alarm 40 to watch`). Plain words: "tells every watch within 40 m".
- **A way up** (`nav.gd` `way`, `folk.gd` `_ladders`/`_climb`): a design's `way X Y Z X Y Z` (two places of it, in its own frame) is a navigation link on a layer of its own, for those on two feet with hands (those who open doors); they climb it, a rung's pace, and go on. The ladders the house and town tools build say one by themselves (host `build.rs`). A dog or a deer has no way up it.

**Checked by script.** `-Demo perceives` (7 beats): the new behaviours read with nothing wrong, deer_ways said in plain words "the player or hunter"; the kinds written with a `way` among a design's lines and things given their own lines (`tags watch`, `hears 12`); a wolf put 7 m from a deer: it ran from the wolf (16.8 m further off in 2 s) and settled to grazing when the wolf was gone, then ran from the walker by the same words; someone who looks into noises heard the dog at a run ("on hears dog anyone creature") and went to look; the dog followed the walker up seven steps to a landing 1.4 m up; on a lookout 2.5 m high, the villager who follows climbed its ladder after them ("Someone of the village climbed up the ladder.") and the dog stayed at its foot; the first of four guards spotted the walker and told the alarm "to watch (2 heard)": the two tagged watch answered, the fourth went on with its patrol; thirty bodies awake and behaving, five seconds: frames 8.2 ms on average, 17 ms at worst, the behaviours 0.21 ms a frame on average and 5.4 ms at the worst frame. No script errors; passed twice after the last changes. Also passing: -Demo guard (its alarm now tells 'to anyone (3 heard)'), -Demo bell, -Demo actions, and the host tests (88 unit, among them a ladder's way and the words tags and way; 101 protocol). -Demo behave passes; its check that 200 more behaving take under 0.5 ms a frame failed three times at first (0.51 to 0.67 ms, against 0.35 to 0.45 ms for the committed scripts on the same machine): a whom said by what it counts as looked through every thing of the world when no one of that sort was about. Mended (those words are never looked for among things; each one's plain name kept): then 0.57, 0.26 and 0.30 ms. The measure is noisy run to run and may go over 0.5 ms now and then, as the committed scripts' 0.45 shows.

Mended on the way: a follower stopped near enough a metre and a half under whom it follows (at the foot of the steps): it is near only on their level now (within 0.6 m up or down).

**Not done here.** Wading costs more than walking only as it slows the body: the ways are one cost throughout (Godot gives a navigation mesh one cost; water would have to be baked as regions of its own, about twice the baking). Swimming is only of what swims without a body (`wild.gd`); no body goes through deep water. The steps of a stair inside a drawn house were not walked by the dog here (the demo's flight is a design of boxes); a house's flights under 4 m cells are too steep, as recorded before. Climbing has no move of its own (the body is carried up the ladder).

### G6, items, stacks, recipes and a chest (2026-10-22)

The next in the user's order (G3, PW0, G4, PW1, G6, G5), from the gameplay roadmap's G6 (`Draw3D_Gameplay_Roadmap_2026-10-21.md`): "gather wood, craft a torch at a bench, equip it, it lights; saved and loaded", and the items tour mended. Nothing of it is tried by hand.

**The items tour mended.** It had failed since 2026-10-16 on a script error at the lantern. The cause was in the tour, not the engine: walking to the lantern the way it did, the walker looked at the hatchet a metre on, and what is at hand is what is looked toward (`acts.gd` `_nearest`, since 7cb), so E picked up the hatchet. The tour now comes to the lantern from the side away from the hatchet. `-Tour -Only items`: no problems, no script errors.

**What was built.**
- **Recipes** (`recipes.txt`, `recipebook.gd`): `recipe NAME` with `called`, `at WORD` (made at what says `crafts WORD`), `uses GOOD N` (used up), `needs GOOD N` (kept), `makes DESIGN [N]` (things, each an item of its own) or `gives GOOD N` (goods), `says`. Four at a bench: a torch (a piece of wood, a piece of scrap), a lockpick, a crate, a barrier of planks (the last two put down in play, PW1b).
- **A bench** (`crafts WORD`, a new word of a design or of one thing's own lines; the act `craft`, act line `crafting`): E at it opens the inventory "At the bench": what is made there, each with what it wants and, greyed, why not yet ("you have no pieces of wood, and a piece of wood is wanted"); Make makes it. Library: `bench-crafting`; Make it usable: "a bench".
- **Items made in play** (`crafting.gd`): a thing made is an entry of the world's fact `made` ([id, design], an id of its own), `where` "kept" and `found` as anything picked up. What it is (its lines and mesh) is asked of the host (`design_made`) and given to `things.gd` as an item from no cell (`carried_in`, as one carried from another world is), so it is held, lit, used, dropped and picked up as any item. Kept by a saved game; none left when the world stops. Library: `torch` (kept, held, lights, taken).
- **Stacks**: things of one sort in the pack are one row ("A torch  x2"); the first of them is what a button does.
- **A chest** (`stores`, a new word; the act `store`, act line `storing`): E at it opens the inventory "In the chest": its goods and the items in it, and the walker's goods to put in; Take and Put in move one at a time, and a thing of the pack chosen is put in. Its goods are its own (`has.GOOD` about it, as a stall's); an item in it is `where` "in ID", not drawn and not in the pack. Library: `chest-wood`; Make it usable: "a store".
- **Wood**: the act line `yields GOOD N` (the doer is given N, from nothing); `fell` yields two pieces of wood; `wood` in goods.txt.
- **The Inspector** says what `crafts` and `stores` mean among a thing's lines.

**Checked by script.** `-Demo crafting` (6 beats): an oak felled, two pieces of wood; E at the chest, two pieces of scrap taken one at a time, one left; E at the bench, four recipes listed, a torch made twice, the pack shows one row of two, a third "Not yet" and why; one held (Hold) and used: lit, its light in the hand at 21:00; the other put in the chest, not in the pack; saved, stopped, started, loaded: the torch held and lit and drawn in the hand, the other in the chest, the scrap left in the chest, both made things there; stopped, nothing made left. Regressions: `-Tour -Only items`, `-Demo inventory`, `shelter`, `remembers`, `actions` pass; host tests 87 unit, 101 protocol (p43 reads the new library designs).

**Not done here.** A recipe's own time to make, and making at a bench by someone of the folk (a sequence step). Several of a good moved at once into a chest (one at a time now). What is put down in play taken up again. Goods have no weight or room in the pack.

### PW1b, a region that remembers: changes that stay (2026-10-22), and a pond on a slope

The second part of PW1 (`Draw3D_Roadmap_Progress_and_Next_Milestone_2026-10-22.md`, §6.2), after PW1a was committed (1328a29) at the user's word, with the user's finding that a pond drawn at random does not fill. Nothing of it is tried by hand.

**A pond on a slope.** A pond dug into the land lowered the land inside it by its depth everywhere, and its water stood a hand under the lowest of its edge. On flat land that is right; on a slope the downhill edge is lower than the dug middle, so the water was under its bed and none was made (the user's random pond). Now its bed is cut level from the lowest of its edge (`Shape::sunk`, the edge's lowest height worked out once in `dug_in`), the land over that cut down over the same shore so the uphill side is a bank rather than a cliff; on flat land the pond is exactly as before. What floats, wades and stands on its water asks the pond's level (`Shape::pond`) instead of the depth dug. Checked by a land test (`a_pond_dug_on_a_slope_holds_water`, which picks a slope where the old dig left the middle over the water) and a new beat of `-Demo details` (a pond dug on a hillside: its middle 0.8 m under its water); `details`, `context` (the dock) and `streets` (bridges over ponds) pass.

**What was built.**
- **Put down in play** (`placed.gd`, case 4): a good that says `puts DESIGN` (goods.txt: `barrier`, `crate`) is put down from the inventory ("Put down") before the walker, turned as they face. Each is an entry of the world's fact `placed` ([id, design, x, y, z, degrees], an id of its own), so it is kept with a saved game and gone when the world stops, never an edit of the document. It is drawn from its design (the host's `design_made`, now also giving its collider), only in active regions; it is solid in its cell (`solid.gd` asks `in_cell`), so its cell's ways are made again and those who go about go round it. Library: `barrier-planks`, `crate-plain` (Shelter).
- **A tree felled** (case 1): the act `fell` (acts.txt: chopped at, then `where gone`); a thing with `where gone` is not drawn, not walked into and not the walker's (`things.gd`). Offered by `offers fell trunk` and `point trunk 0 1 0`: on a kind for every tree of a wood, or one tree by the Inspector's Make it usable, "a tree" (uses.txt).
- **Goods moved by someone** (case 5): the behaviour `fetches` (behaviours.txt: go to a store and do an act there, again and again; the flour sacks by default).
- **A crop that grows while no one is by**: a timer (`ticks NAME S`) that goes out of reach keeps how far it was and the world's hour; made again, the time away is counted in the world's hours (an hour a minute), if its `when` holds then (`loose.gd` `_caught_up`); kept with a saved game (`waits`). Before, a timer that went out of reach lost its count and nothing ticked while away.
- **A wood sown again** (criterion 5): a saved game now says where each thing it has facts about stood and the seed of the maker that made it (core `Stood`). Loaded where that maker has another seed and the thing of that id stands more than a metre away, its facts are set aside under an id of their own (`State::set_aside`), applied to nothing, and listed (`elsewhere`; the load message and Playtest say "made again somewhere else"). Moved by hand, its maker's seed the same, a thing keeps its facts (p11). Host test p98 (fails without it).
- **Crossings timed**: `regions.gd` keeps the longest frame in the second after each region change (`crossings`); Playtest's Regions says it, and how many things were put down in play in each region.

**Checked by script.** `-Demo remembers` (7 beats) on an island of 512 m: in the east the player fells an oak, opens a gate, picks up and drops an axe, puts down a crate from the pack, shoves a light crate; a villager fetches flour. A barrier put down across a lane: the way between went through it (10.1 m) and within 0.09 s goes round it (10.6 m). Walked away at seven, back at ten: all six as left by fact and by what is drawn and solid, the crate within 0.01 m of where it came to rest, the barley grew 3 ticks for 3 hours away, the way still goes round. Saved far off, the world stopped and started, loaded: the same. The wood given another seed before a load: the felled oak's fact set aside and listed; the oak with its number now stands. Ten crossings of a region's edge: the slowest frame in the second after each 6.9 to 8.4 ms. No problems, no script errors. Host tests: 87 unit, 101 protocol. Regressions: `-Demo regions`, `guard`, `behave`, `signals`, `inventory`, `actions`, `rules1` pass.

**Measured, and what it says.** The crossings were timed in a `-Check` run, whose window is hidden and whose frames are held to 144 a second (6.9 ms): the numbers say no crossing came near 33 ms on this machine, not how a crossing feels in a busy world (a world of few things was crossed). Deciding a crossing took under 0.1 ms; letting go of a few creatures 0.6 to 3.4 ms (PW1a).

**Not done here.** Whether far regions stop being drawn (mesh bytes do not go down by region; far land is drawn coarser; that is a visible draw distance and the user's decision). What is put down in play cannot be taken up again yet (G6 or building while playing). Felling needs no tool and leaves no stump. Ten crossings of a populated region (a hamlet with folk) are not measured. A timer's `when` is asked once, as it comes near, for the whole time away.

### PW1a, regions that let go and remember (2026-10-22): the first part of "a region that remembers"

The first part of PW1 (`Draw3D_Roadmap_Progress_and_Next_Milestone_2026-10-22.md`, §6.2), after G4 in the user's order. Nothing of it is tried by hand.

**What was already only about the walker.** Reading the code first: what is solid is built only in the cells about whoever walks (`solid.gd`); what is loose is a body only there (`loose.gd`); the ways are made only for the cells asked for (`nav.gd`); what is drawn is drawn in coarser regions farther off (`world_view.gd`). What was not: everyone who goes about (`folk.gd`) was made a full body (bones, mesh, motor) in every cell of the world as play began, and only stood still beyond 75 m. That is what PW1a lets go.

**What was built.**
- **Regions** (`regions.gd`): while the world runs, squares of 4 × 4 cells (128 m); the walker's region and those beside it are active, the rest far. Looked at four times a second; each change told in the run log with how long it took ("The walker is in region 1,-1: 6 active, 10 far; 1 let go; … near again (0.8 ms)").
- **Let go and made again** (`folk.gd` `let_go_far`, `dormant`): whoever goes about in a far region has where they stand and (if hurt) their health put as facts, and their body taken away; they are not drawn where they were made meanwhile. When their region is active they are made from their cell by the same code that made them first, and stand where the facts say. Those who walk into a far region are let go within 2 s. Not let go: one in an act, and one the eye is watching through. What behaves lets go and takes up its state again, by facts (`rules.gd` says "is far off: let go until its region is near").
- **Catch-up, first tier**: one whose day says where to be by the hour (`goes`) and whose hour has come round while they were let go is made where their day says now ("The miller was far off and is now where their day says (10:00)."); not what they would have done on the way.
- **Health kept**: a hurt one's health is now the fact `health` about it, put when it is let go and when the game is saved, and read back (`fight.gd`). Before, a wounded enemy came back whole after a load.
- **Playtest, Regions**: what Godot holds (nodes, moving bodies, those who go about and those let go, mesh MB) and each region: its state, its things, how many have facts, awake / asleep / let go, its last change and its milliseconds. "Show them on the ground" draws each region's edge at the walker's height, green active, grey far, with its name.

**Checked by script.** -Demo regions (7 beats), on an island of 512 m (16 regions): the deer in the east are not made while the walker is in the west; walked east they are made and the west's miller is let go; walked away and back, each deer is made within 0.01 m of where it was let go; back at ten after leaving at seven, the miller is 0.4 m from where their day says; saved and loaded while far, the deer again within 0.01 m. Letting go took 3.4 ms for six deer, coming near 0.8 ms. No problems, no script errors. Run again after it: -Demo guard 9/9, behave 14/14, rules1, journey, and -Tour -Only villagers: no problems, no script errors. -Tour -Only saves: the saved game 'quick' loads (11 facts) but the walker is not on the ground within 7 s; that save is from 17 October, of another world seen side-on (the walker at -10, 6, 0, 3 things gone), not the old stage-5 save the tour was written for (Known gaps).

**Measured, and what it says.** In the editor Godot holds about 4,800 nodes, most of them the editor's own windows; six deer made add about 40, and back in the west the count is within 0.4% of where it began. So in a world of a few creatures the bodies are a small part of what Godot holds: the regions are what keeps a world of many from growing with it, and the measure that matters more is a populated world (PW1b). Mesh bytes held do not go down when regions are far (16.8 MB throughout): what is drawn is not let go by region, by choice: far regions are drawn coarser, and letting them go would make the land beyond 200 m disappear. That trade is for the user to decide with numbers (PW1b).

**Not done here (PW1b, next).** Things the player puts down in play (case 4) and the ways round them; where a pushed crate rests across a far region (case 6); a reseeded wood keeping what it can; ten crossings measured for hitches; all six of the player's changes checked across unload and across save and load; a crop's ticking fact over the time away; whether far regions stop being drawn.

### G4, one act for every doer (2026-10-22): Do an act in behaviours, an act's condition, the village tour mended

G4 of the gameplay roadmap, after PW0 in the order the user set. Nothing of it is tried by hand.

**What was already so.** Acts (`acts.txt`, `acts.gd`) were already one definition done by the player's E / Y and by the folk's days (`work.gd` begins the same act with a villager's body). The acts the roadmap's first set names mostly exist: open, shut, unlock (by key or lockpick), pick up, put down, take, search, talk, sit, sleep, eat, push, kick. What was missing: a behaviour could not do an act, an act could only be conditioned on one fact (`while`, `unless`) and goods, and the village tour failed.

**What was built.**
- **Do an act, a behaviour step** (`act ACT WHAT`, or `act ACT at WHAT`): the nearest thing called so that offers the act now is gone to and the act is done with it by `acts.gd`'s own code, as the player's E does it (the walk to where it is done from, the act's move and hand, what it puts, and the event `act` raised for whatever behaves at the thing). Not done, with why, when nothing near offers it (`not_now`'s words: shut already, locked, its condition not so). In the Behaviours window it is "Do an act", with a list of the acts; in plain words "goes and does “open” at the gate". `rules.gd` `_start_act` / `_tick_act`.
- **An act's condition**, `when CONDITION` in acts.txt: any of `cond.gd`'s words (hour, has, its, fact, weather, near, all:, any:, `walker ...`), asked of the thing, as `while` and `unless` are. When it does not hold the act is not offered and the player is told why in plain words: "Open the gate? It is 21:00, not between 06:00 and 20:00." A villager or a behaviour is refused with the same words. Checked as acts.txt is read (`actbook.gd`). The Inspector's How it is done says each offered act's condition ("open: only when it is between 06:00 and 20:00").
- **Content:** the act `open_by_day` (`when hour 6 20`); library designs `gate-plain` (opened and shut by hand or by a behaviour) and `gate-by-day` (Shelter); the behaviour `opens_for_you` (a porter: when the player comes within 8 m it opens the gate, says "In you come.", and shuts it once they are 12 m off).
- **The village tour mended** (`-Tour -Only village`). Its walking part (doors opened with E, room to room, the baker's yard) already passed. Its building part failed because the Build list gained a drawn house, "A house: drag it out…", above the house on cells, so the tour's search for "A house:" took the wrong one and then crashed on a Makers button that a drawn house has none of. The tour now picks the rows by their full words and says walls inside from the Build list's "Walls inside the structure chosen" (one place per job, U5). It passes: walked, built, roofed, a pond, all undone, the showcase file untouched.

**Checked by script.**
- **-Demo actions** (7 beats): read; put down and given in the window; the porter opens the gate by the act open when the walker comes near (its act ended as done, "In you come."), the walker goes through, the porter shuts it by the act shut; by day the gate by day is offered and opened by hand; at night it says why and pressing does nothing; the strongbox says "Unlock the strongbox? You have no strongbox key." and with the key is unlocked and the key kept. 7 of 7, no script errors; its pictures looked at.

**Different from the roadmap.**
- No `actions.txt`: acts.txt already was the one definition the player and the folk share, so it stays, and the new words were added to it (no file renamed, nothing rewritten).
- Not built: an act's own duration and interruption (`takes` as seconds of work, `interrupted by`), `then` a state, and a `lock` act. Acts last as long as their move; lock-picking already has its own move.

### PW0, saved games that keep up (2026-10-22): facts follow renamed things, what is gone is listed, a guard's search is kept

The first step of the persistent-world milestone (`Draw3D_Roadmap_Progress_and_Next_Milestone_2026-10-22.md`, §6.2), in the order the user set at the checkpoint (G3, PW0, G4, PW1, G6, G5). Nothing of it is tried by hand.

**What was wrong.** A saved game names things by id. When a maker's code renames what it makes (an upgrade with a declared id migration), the document records where every old id went, but `load` never asked: the facts stayed on the old ids and applied to nothing, counted as "gone". The assessment had found this by search; host test p97 confirms it (it fails with the following taken out). Facts about things really gone were counted but not said, and a guard's `noticed` place lived only in `rules.gd`, so a guard loaded mid-search had nowhere to go and gave up.

**What was built.**
- **A saved game says how many id migrations its world had** (`migrations`, core `state.rs`). Loading carries each fact through the document's `resolve_id` from that number (`State::follow`): renamed, it goes to the new id; split, to each; no successor, it stays where it was. A game saved before this, which does not say, is carried through all migrations, but only for ids not in the world now. Journeys do the same for each world.
- **What is gone is listed, not lost or misapplied.** The host's `load` answers `followed` (things renamed since) and `orphans` (the first 40 things not in the world, each with the names of its facts, and whether a migration said it has no successor), beside `missing`. Their facts are kept under the old id, applied to nothing.

### G3, the bell at the gate (2026-10-22): one event heard by a thing and a person; behaviours said in plain words first

The gameplay roadmap's G3 vertical slice, started straight after the checkpoint as the user's sequence says (G3 → PW0 → …).

**Built:**

  - the act `ring` (acts.txt: a hand to the rope; `says ring`, so it is offered as "ring the bell");
  - the good `lantern` (goods.txt; a counted good, kept in a saved game; a lantern *item* is G6's);
  - three behaviours in behaviours.txt;
  - three library designs that come with their behaviour (`behaves` on the design): `gate-ruled` and `bell-post` in Shelter, `gatekeeper` in Watchers. A gatekeeper is a guard's body, with no eyes for hunting.
- **The three behaviours:**
  - `bell_rope`: rung, it sounds and `tell ring 30`.
  - `day_gate`: shut. Told `ring` between {opens} and {shuts}, it opens, otherwise it says {night_says}; tried, it says "Ring the bell."; open, it shuts `on hour {shuts}`.
  - `gate_keeper`: patrols its post. Told `ring`, it says "Coming!", goes to the walker, says {greets} and gives {gift} the first time, then remembers `done_giving` (its own fact). After that it says {again}, and goes back to its post.
- **Plain words first in Behaviours and rules** (the checkpoint's finding; `Draw3D_Behaviour_Wording_Research_2026-10-22.md`):
  - `plainrules.gd` says a behaviour as a person would: "While it is Shut (it begins so) / When it is told “ring”: if it is between 06:00 and 20:00: changes to Open; otherwise: says “Come back by day.”", with its settings filled in.
  - It is shown as **What it does** under the description.
  - The states and steps are folded under **▸ Show the details (states and steps)**, opened by the button and by itself when a step is chosen.
  - "Needs: to react to 'act'" now reads "to be used by the player (E / Y)".
- **A real defect found and mended** (`rules.gd` `_world_events`):
  - A behaviour's `on hour H` fired only if the hour was passed on the very frame that thing looked: things look every LOOK seconds, but the hour was remembered every frame.
  - Each now remembers the hour as it last looked (`e["hour_was"]`).
  - Found by the gate not shutting at eight. The G1 wires (`events.gd`) were not affected.

**What differs from the roadmap's G3, and why:**
- The gate is a placed design between two placed walls, not a drawn wall's gate. Giving behaviours to drawn structures' doors and gates is G4's action model.
- The lantern is a counted good, not an item in the hand (G6).
- "Two gates given the rule" is done on two placed doors given `day_gate` in one step.
- **The demo's walls are short.** At night the keeper walks round them to the walker, instead of stopping behind the shut gate, and the caption says so.

  - `erasable` counts painted ground in square metres of each surface.
  - Erase has **paint on the ground (snow N m²)**, ticked by default; "which" lists "only snow on the ground".
  - Terrain > Paint says **Painted in this world now: snow N m²**.

Anything over painted snow that faces up is white, in the same way weather snow lies: a roof, a rock, a crate. What a roof shelters stays bare.

A word that may be said more than once (`spins`) was not replaced, so the + wrote a new line with no part in it, and the picked part kept spinning at 30. `abilities.set_line` now replaces the line it changed (`write(..., instead)`).

  - The + for a corner, the wings and the corner towers fade in only as the pointer comes near.
  - Entering play now selects nothing and clears every line and house handle (`main.play`).

  - A structure has a new look word, **`door_keeps`**: "" (opened in play), `open` (it stands open, `when not never`) or `shut` (nothing to open it by).

### U2 of the usability audit: the Behaviour card and the Inspector's order (2026-10-22; after the user's hand test of U1)

**The user's hand test of U1:** the wording is better. But they deleted Run away (and a second behaviour, the locked door) and had no way to make them again; "Add from library does nothing"; behaviours must never be permanently deleted. The Settings hint ("No settings. A number in a step can be made a setting") is unnecessary. For a later pass: no way to see every animal or character in the world at once, nor a list of them (recorded in the audit, beside U3). Then: "sort out and continue to the next pass".

**The cause, and the mend:**
- In the editor every behaviour change is written straight into `godot/behaviours.txt` (`keeps_texts`), and that same file was "the library". So Delete removed a behaviour from the library too, and Add from library compared the world with itself and never found anything to add.
- **Restored:** `door_lock` and `run_away`, from this session's own earlier reads of the file (the file is untracked, so git had no copy), with U1's wording ("tried by the player with its key").
- **Your library of behaviours** is now a file of its own, `editor/library/behaviours/behaviours.txt` (seeded with the five; the host's design library reads only the folder's top level, so it does not read this). Save to library saves the behaviour shown into it. Add from library ▾ lists the library's behaviours this world lacks, one by one or all. Delete keeps a copy there first and says so; a behaviour that other behaviours or objects use is named first, and goes on a second press. The editor never takes anything out of the library. A script can point the window at a scratch library (`library_at`), so demos never write the person's.
- **Settings:** shown only when a behaviour has some. Add a setting is under the steps, with two fields (Setting name, Usual value).

  - its description, a red line for what it cannot do yet, and its settings inline, set for this one or every one as chosen.
  Draw3D's own objects (a barrel) have no type text, so Every is not offered for them; the window's Apply to every says why instead of failing on a host error.

- **Placement, Physics, Advanced** are folds below. Advanced holds the links to text (Edit type as text…, Behaviours window…, Signals…, Its layout…), the lines of what and where it is, its layout's settings, freeze and another seed. Whether each fold is open is kept for the person (`user://inspector.cfg`). With nothing selected, or a layout chosen from the list at the top, nothing is folded.
- **The Behaviours window** begins on the behaviour: its list, Behaviour ▾ (New…, Copy…, Rename…, Delete, Save to library, Import from text…), Add from library ▾; a name row shows only for New, Copy and Rename. Selected and its Apply buttons follow the needs.

### Editor usability and cognitive complexity audit (2026-10-21, after 7dh; nothing built)

From the user's brief after trying a "run away" behaviour on the ranger: a code-grounded audit of the editor's wording, concepts and decisions, `Draw3D_Editor_Usability_Audit_2026-10-21.md`. No code was changed. Evidence: the GDScript that draws each label (quoted with file and line), the scripted demos' screenshots in `editor/godot/demo/`, and the user's own report; the live editor was not driven by hand. Six root causes (a private writing voice on every control; ids and file names shown by default; several systems for one outcome, such as three for running away and four for a door; the this-one-or-every-one scope asked first; everything shown at once; Build, Paint, Erase and the world's look each in two to four places), ten findings, a term table, eight tasks before and after (snow cannot be painted, one part cannot spin, no door preset: engineering gaps), a proposed interface standard of thirteen rules, stages U0–U6 and acceptance criteria. U0 is the user's: their terms maker / arrangement / thing / sort, merging the toolbars, painted against weather snow, per-part spin. Nothing is to be built until they decide.

### The guard: patrol, hear, investigate, alarm, back to the round (2026-10-22, amendment 7di; G2's third example)

At the user's brief after commit 9414904, which changed only the window's abilities line among the behaviour files. Nothing was downloaded or committed.

**Built and auto-checked:**

- **General additions, each in `rulebook.gd`'s registry and offered by the window:**
  - the event `hears [WHAT]` (`watch.gd` raises it at most once a second, not for the thing's own noises, with where the noise was made);
  - the place `noticed` (where it last heard a noise, saw the walker, or was told from);
  - the steps `patrol` (its design's `patrols`, the same round `watch.gd` keeps), `look_about S` and `hurry WHERE` (as `go`, at a run);
  - a needs line may name several words; "a round to patrol" is said;
  - the event `catches`, raised by `watch.gd` for the guard that caught the walker. At the user's decision, `watch.gd` `calm` no longer sends a guard whose legs a behaviour has home or begins its round again: the stealth game decides the catch, the behaviour what the guard does after (`guard_ways`: "Got you.", back to its round). Guards with no such behaviour go home as before.

  - **Caught:** the walker stood still and was caught: counted once, the world's `caught` put, the walker back where they were safe. The guard heard `catches`, said "Got you." and went back to its round from where it stood, 11 m from home. No guard moved more than 0.1 m in a frame afterwards, and its round was not begun again.
